old_title: Live: Rabbitohs ravaging Roosters' reserves after Jai Arrow makes tearful 100th Souths appearance
new_title: Jai Arrow makes emotional 100th Souths appearance, Souths thrash Roosters
old_text:
live
NRL live: Jai Arrow's 100th Rabbitohs game against Roosters
Jai Arrow walks out with the Rabbitohs for the 100th time against rivals the Roosters at a sold out Sydney Football Stadium.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, check out all the stats in the full ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

Live updates
Live updates: Souths vs Roosters

Dolphins hang on to beat the Titans
The Dolphins led 12-0 inside the opening 10 minutes and 14-12 at the break, but despite a late surge could not beat the finals-bound Dolphins, who claimed a tense 20-24 victory at Robina.
Jayden Campbell and AJ Brimson gave the Titans a brilliant start, before Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Herbie Farnworth fought back before the break.
The Dolphins looked to kick away early in the second term with tries to Ray Stone and Tabuai-Fidow.
But the Titans fought back, Campbell scoring a second in game 100 to make it 20-24.
The hosts came desperately close to levelling things late on, but a last-minute sin binning to Moeaki Fotuaika ended the Titans' hopes, despite the home crowd believing with some justification that the sin binning was not only harsh, but should have been been shown to at least one Dolphin, with a very late shot and a trip going unpunished.
Key Event
HT: Souths powering past youthful Roosters
An emotional start to the night.
And the emotion almost threatened to boil over at times in that first half, with Spencer Leniu at the heart of all the problems.
But the Roosters, undermanned after making 10 changes, are perhaps not even second best in this game.
They trail 20-4 and the Rabbitohs are making mince meat out of these Roosters ring ins.
This could get even uglier, as the Rabbitohs seem set to secure a home final.
36' Roosters blow a promising position
Cody Ramsey made a magnificent break from the back after fielding a monster of a bomb from Latrell Mitchell.
He made 40 metres up field as the Roosters got on the front foot.
But then Toby Rodwell passed the ball forward and the chance goes begging.
33' Try Souths!
Campbell Graham finishes off the move with typical aplomb down the right side for the Rabbitohs.
Good passing down the line, Walker to Wighton, who caught and threw in one motion to send Graham into space.
He still had work to do, but stepped off his right and then his left, darting over from 10 metres out.
The kick from the sideline is good from Mitchell - haven't we had a mixed bag from him off the tee tonight - and it's 20-4.
32' Try-saver by the Roosters
Rex Bassingthwaighte saves a try with a brilliant tackle on a rampaging Latrell Mitchell!
Cam Murry sparked the move by swooping like a sea gull on a chip as a loose pass found turf in front of him.
He passed to Mitchell who looked certain to score until Bassingthwaighte leaped onto his back and hauled the giant centre down.
30' Penalty Souths
Another penalty foes the way of Souths, it's Spencer Leniu who gives it away for a high tackle as the Rabbitohs pound the Roosters line inside the 10.
The Rabbitohs move the ball left but Mitchell throws a horror of a pass to Johnston and the chance goes begging on that side of the field.
Key Event
26' 'No more!'
Adam Gee has had enough!
It's Latrell Mitchell this time who nearly takes a Rooster's head off in back play and it is game on all over the place.
The referee calls both captains over and says the next time the teams come together it's going to be a sin bin special.
He specifically calls out Spencer Leniu and tells him "no more".,
This game is heated!
25' Penalty Souths!
The Roosters prop is, and I say this in the nicest way I can, a complete idiot.
A liability.
Spencer Leniu has thrown the ball away and squared up to Koloamatagi and given away the penalty.
It's stupid.
24' LENIU IS SMASHED!
OH MY WORD!
Spencer Leniu from kick off takes the ball and he has been belted by Keon Koloamatangi!
David Fifita is there too and he put one on the Roosters prop as well.
AND NOW THEY'RE INTO IT AGAIN!
AND LENIU AND KOLOAMATANGI SQUARE UP!
23' Try Roosters!
The Roosters have made the most of their slice of luck!
A simple left-side shift and Daniel Tupou is on hand to score in the corner.
It was pretty simple, but you only need to give Tupou an inch for him to squirm through.
The kick is missed and it's 14-4.
22' Roosters 40:20!
That's a brilliant kick from Toby Rodwell!
He was well inside the 40 - but did he kick it into the 20?!
The referee Adam Gee says yes, but that replay makes it look like he was a matter of centimetres short.
The touch judge says that it wasn't... but he was overruled.
Hmmmmm.
19' Roosters challenge
Alex Johnston makes a break and kicks the ball off the outside of his right foot infield to Mitchell, who can't get there in time as the Roosters bat it back.
The Roosters challenge an obstruction non-call that helped create the move when Cody Walker bounced off a couple of his own players in midfield.
But it's not obstruction!
The Roosters burn their challenge early.
17' Alex Johnston has his 30th try for the year
My word that was as easy as it comes.
Souths pass the ball to the left, it goes through a couple of pairs of hands, Latrell Mitchell just nonchalantly dishing it off to Alex Johnston and it is as simple as that for Alex Johnston.
It is the third time in his career that he has scored 30 tries.
Latrell Mitchell misses the kick from the left sideline.
It's 14-0.
16' Penalty Souths
Egan Butcher catches Cam Murray high in a tackle and the Rabbitohs have a penalty on the 40, which they kick to the 30 to start another set.
The momentum all with the Rabbitohs.
14' Souths score again!
Given the team lists, this is not a surprise.
Cameron Murray held the ball up, Keaon Koloamatangi was the decoy, Jayden Sullivan made the run and scrambled over the line under the posts.
It came after the Roosters completely fluffed a goal line drop out, Toby Rodwell just getting his angles all wrong - he nearly hit the post instead of it going 10 metres.
The kick is good from Mitchell and it's 10-0.
11' Penalty Souths
Spencer Leniu crashed into Cody Walker hard and late and provoked the ire of the referee as a result.
Penalty Souths 30 metres out.
10' Try saver from Jye Gray
Rex Bassingthwaighte gets the ball on the wing - without being too disrespectful you could almost imagine the ball in the hands of Mark Nawaqanitawase if you squint thanks to the excess hair.
But you'd need to squint pretty hard.
Bassingthwaighte tucks the ball under his arm but is denied by Jye Gray, powering into the winger and knocking the ball lose and the man into touch.
6' Try Souths!
How on earth has David Fifita managed to get the ball down there!
In his 150th NRL game, he has powered his way into three Roosters players out of dummy half and somehow managed to ground the ball.
Fifita has started brightly, he's already made 30 metres from three runs, and that was the best of them, running over one defender and shrugging off the other two to score.
Latrell Mitchell hooks the kick wide and it remains 4-0.
3' Roosters challenge early
Egan Butcher loses the ball in the tackle but immediately asks for a review.
Cody Walker is, as one can understand, a bit reluctant to challenge, but he does and it's the right call.
Brandon Smith is pinged for the strip.
new_text:
Jai Arrow makes his 100th Rabbitohs appearance, South Sydney beat Roosters 50-22 to secure home NRL final
Tears flowed as Jai Arrow made his 100th Rabbitohs appearance, with his Souths teammates helping crush the reserve team of their arch rivals, the Roosters.
Arrow choked back tears when he was hugged by Wayne Bennett as the forward was given a hero's reception at a sold out Sydney Football Stadium.
The 31-year-old father of one was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) this year and, until two weeks ago, was stranded on 98 NRL games for the Bunnies.
At Bennett's initiative, the NRL allowed Souths an extra interchange against the Gold Coast last week for game number 99 and again on Friday against the Roosters.
"It was pretty emotional," Cam Murray told Channel 9.
"I'm just so happy that everyone was able to get around him and he's been able to feel all the love.
"I know he really appreciates it and we love to see it.
"We all love him and happy he was able to notch up 100 games."
Arrow led his teammates out to the sound of the Gerry and the Pacemakers rendition of You'll Never Walk Alone, with 14th Immortal and dual-club legend Ron Coote ringing the Rabbitohs' bell.
The former Queensland State of Origin forward was given a guard of honour by more than 100 Souths old boys, including members of the 2021 grand final squad Arrow was a member of and his family, who all sobbed along with him and plenty of others in the stands.
"It was emotional," Roosters captain Connor Watson said in his post-match press conference.
"It was very touching. Things like that are bigger than rugby league."
In the subsequent match, the Rabbitohs ran in 10 tries to pummel the Roosters 50-20, who had rested 10 of their star players with a top four spot secure.
But in completing the win, Souths have themselves earned a home finals spot, and will face Newcastle at either the Olympic Stadium or Sydney Football Stadium next week.
Campbell Graham scored twice for the Rabbitohs, who had nine different try scorers on the night, including Alex Johnston, who crossed for the 30th time this season.
Latrell Mitchell was one of them, scoring on his return to the starting line up while mixing his sublime skill with fearsome physicality, most notably when he flattened Toby Rodwell in the closing stages, standing over the stricken half like Mohammed Ali over Sonny Liston in their 1965 rematch.
If Mitchell's performance was heartening - a poor 5/10 kicking rate aside - Roosters firebrand Spencer Leniu will have raised concerns from coach Trent Robinson in the first half.
Leniu squared up to Keaon Koloamatangi after the Rabbitohs prop smashed him in a tackle twice in the same set, the second time tossing the ball away and giving away a penalty.
Titans fume over questionable calls
Earlier, the Dolphins hung on to beat the Titans 24-20 on the Gold Coast.
It was the Dolphins' seventh-consecutive win, but almost didn't happen as the Titans fought back late on and were unfortunate not to come away with the win.
The Titans were left fuming when, while leading 14-0, they had Keano Kini sin-binned in the 23rd minute for a very soft push on Dolphins winger Tevita Naufahu.
Josh Hannay was fuming after that call, and a trio of others in the closing minutes, went against his side.
"I thought it was incredibly harsh and not long after that they get a try from a knock-on," Hannay said.
"You talk about momentum swings - they don't get much bigger than that. Moe [Moeaki Fotuaika] got smacked in the face at the end and ends up in the bin for retaliating.
"[Jamayne Isaako] throws a leg out to trip [AJ Brimson] in the act of a potential try-scoring play and it is just a penalty.
"It was probably more sin-binnable than Keano's play.
"You stack all those things up and you lose by four points, you have got to be proud of your team's effort."
With AAP

Time to say goodnight
Well, it's been a big day.
Jai Arrow has played 100 NRL games for South Sydney.
The outpouring of support from the NRL community has been stunning.
As so many people have said, some things are bigger than rugby league.
This was one of those things.
We'll be back tomorrow, I hope you'll join us then.
Jai Arrow moment 'very touching': Watson
Connor Watson is speaking about what it felt like to be out there today during the Jai Arrow moment pre-game.
"It was emotional," Watson says.
"It was very touching. Things like that are bigger than rugby league.
"It's definitely an experience to be part of something so moving.
"The start was very passionate, and it was great to be out there."
Robinson happy with kids display despite defeat
Here's Roosters coach Trent Robinson.
"Those two tries to get back to 20-14 ... I think we had an error off the kick off?" he says.
"I thought our effort was outstanding, I thought the boys worked really hard, they didn't stop, but we had errors at a lot of different times."
He says that he knows people will disagree with his decision to play the kids, but he knows that he got a lot out of it.
"I love the fact that they got to experience that. There's a lot of future out there," he says.
"I thought the experience that they got was great."
He says that Spencer Leniu possibly "went over" the line at times, but he doesn't want to curb his natural "spirit".
"He's got enough experience that he should have regulated it," he says.
"He creates an atmosphere when he's in that mode, aside from [the penalty] I would have liked it to be beneficial to us."
Lots of love for Jai Arrow
Jai Arrow was getting plenty of love from rivals and teammates alike post-match.
'We all love him': Cam Murray hails Jai Arrow
Cam Murray is speaking to Channel Nine after the match.
He's happy with the win, it goes without saying: "It's always good to win against the Roosters," he says.
But the bigger thing was, as always, Jai Arrow.
"It was pretty emotional," he says.
"I'm just so happy that everyone was able to get around him and he's been able to feel all the love.
"I know he really appreciates it and we love to see it.
"We all love him and happy he was able to notch up 100 games."
FT: Souths claim dominant victory
South Sydney have secured a home final, beating the Roosters reserves 50-20 after an emotional night when Jai Arrow was honoured for playing his 100th NRL game for the club.
The Roosters, secure inside the top four, made 10 changes from their first choice team for the match, and it looked like it was to be one way traffic at a sold out Sydney Football Stadium.
The Rabbitohs led 20-4 at half time and pushed that out to 24-4 10 minutes into the second period.
However, the Roosters then fought back with two tries in as many minutes to make things a little nervous for the Bunnies.
But Cody Walker scored to settle the Rabbitohs, who went on to score 10 tries in a dominant display.
Lachlan Hubner and De La Salle Va'a were both sin binned in the last 10 minutes of the game for a brawl on a night where emotions occasionally threatened to boil over.
And Latrell Mitchell was a tad lucky to get away with a monster shot on Toby Rodwell which, had it been any higher, would have seen the Rabbitohs centre in deep trouble with the judiciary.
78' Try Roosters
Rex Bassingthwaighte does another Nawaqanitawase impression by getting onto the end of a cross field kick!
But my word he was given a free path by a pathetic effort from Latrell Mitchell.
Alex Johnston has laid into Mitchell there, which is a surprise in the sense that the game has well and truly gone but not a surprise in the lowering of defensive standards from the star centre.
He backed away and just let the youngster have a free run at the ball, which he accepted and scored.
Weird from Mitchell, just real odd.
It's 50-20.
77' Try Souths!
Brandon Smith crosses and the Rabbitohs have the half century!
Dummy half run from Smith, he tears out from behind the tackle and has powered into contact.
He does so well to get this ball down, staying up after missing one effort and then coming back and going again.
That's a great individual score.
It's 48-14 but the kick is almost dead in front - and not even Mitchell's wayward boot of the evening will miss this.
It's 50-14.
Call this a pummelling.
77' MITCHELL SMASHES RODWELL!
Oh my word what a risk!
Latrell Mitchell has absolutely smashed Toby Rodwell!
He has folded him like an envelope and stood over him like Ali over Liston in 1965.
If Mitchell has strayed a touch high here then he'll be rubbed out for finals - but he's got away with that. A centimetre higher and he would have been sent off.
But we should give him credit for making a hard but fair tackle.
He has flattened him. My word.
Key Event
73' Roosters and Rabbitohs to play final 7 minutes a man down
De La Salle Va'a and Lachlan Hubner have both been sin binned.
Hubner for sparking the brawl, Va'a for carrying on with it.
12 vs 12 to end the game.
72' BIG BLUE!
IT'S ON IN THE CORNER!
Mitchell crashes over in the corner, but there are a few question marks I have about the try.
Spencer Leniu picked up the ball and ran away with it, but he was charged down by a shoulder charge from Lachlan Hubner.
And then it was on!
The try has been confirmed!
That's incredible. Mitchell stole the ball in a strip where there were three players in the tackle at least, then may well have fumbled it over the line.
OK.
The try stands.
The kick is woeful even by the standards of the night, so it stays 44-14.
67' Try Rabbitohs
Campbell Graham with a brilliant touch down in the corner!
That's a brilliant finish!
The kick through was a beauty by Jamie Humphreys, perfectly weighted and it's a great finish in the corner.
The score is 40-14 and that's where it will stay, as Mitchell wildly misses the kick and he's annoyed with himself as a result.
63' PENALTY TRY SOUTHS!
South Sydney gets a penalty try!
Latrell Mitchell came through and looked like he got the ball down.
But they decided that he didn't get downward pressure.
That's OK though, because Adam Elliott was clearly being held back by Tommy Talau and the bunker says that's a penalty try!
Mitchell was behind Elliott when the contact was made but still got to the ball, so the rationale is that Elliott would have got there.
The kick from in front is good.
It's 36-14 and the brief concern among Souths fans has thoroughly dissipated.
I'm glad it's not just me
Rex Bassingthwaighte looks more like Mark Nawaqanitawase than Mark Nawaqanitawase does!
- Mike
I mean, have you ever seen them in the same team together?
60' Penalty Souths
Nasty tackle that one, Benaiah Ioelu picked up Cam Murray and dumped him on his back.
Was he taken beyond the horizontal? Looked close.
Players threaten to come back in, the aggression of earlier in the game rousing itself from its slumber for a moment, but it's defused quickly enough.
59' Another player goes down
Euan Aitkin is down now.
His shoulder may have popped out.
Tommy Talau put a shot on him and Aitkin is in agony!
He is having to come off.
Good news is that Adam Elliot passed his HIA so he's OK to come back on.
57' Souths score!
Cometh the Hour!
Cody Walker does it all himself!
An error from Toby Rodwell as the Roosters looked to make it a triple strike back gave the Rabbitohs the ball in an attacking position on the field.
The Roosters, bubble well and truly pricked, have to get back into defensive mode and can't do it quickly enough, Cody Walker bashing his way over from close range.
The kick is good and it's 30-14.
54' Try Roosters!
Oh my!
Game well and truly on!
A brilliant break by Benaiah Ioelu out of dummy half puts giant prop/concreter Taylor Losalu through!
He finds Egan Butcher in support and he crosses to score!
Two tries in two minutes and the Roosters are well and truly back in this game!
The Rabbitohs have taken their foot off the gas and are being made to pay for it.
The kick is missed - that might be a sucker punch - and it's 24-14.
51' The Roosters score out of nothing!
Great work from the Roosters!
The move started on half way and they shifted it to the right side.
Rex Bassingthwaighte was on the end of the pass on the wing and he showed a clean pair of heels to Jye Gray.
Now you don't have to squint that much at all to see the likeness to Mark Nawaqanitawase, the hairline and style is eerie, and he has the speed of the giant former Wallaby too.
The 19-year-old still has a bit of growing to to though, to be fair.
The kick is good and it's 24-10!
